resources.string: Looking for Macs that can start a stream…
Choose the Mac to connect to.
No Mac found. Open WirelessScreen on a Mac on this WiFi and allow connection requests in its settings.
Could not search for Macs. Check WiFi and Local Network access.
The Mac is still finding this device. Retrying %1$s…
This Mac only accepts requests from known devices. Connect once from the Mac, or turn on “Allow unrecognized devices” in its settings.
Connection requests are off on this Mac. Open WirelessScreen there and turn on “Allow devices to request this Mac”.
The Mac cannot see this device yet. Keep this screen open and try again.
The Mac could not start the connection. Try again.
On the Mac, open WirelessScreen and turn on \"Use this Mac as a display\". Both devices must be on the same WiFi.
No Mac found. Enter its address manually.
That device is not a Mac receiver.
Accessibility is off: the screen is visible, but taps and typing won\'t work.
Could not connect to the Mac: %1$s. Make sure Receive a screen is on, both devices share the same Wi-Fi, and the firewall allows WirelessScreen.
connection refused — is “Receive a screen” enabled on the Mac?
network unreachable — check that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi
Your tablet as a wireless Mac display
Ask a Mac to send its screen here, or share this screen to a Mac window
Share this screen to your Mac
On — click and type from the Mac.
Search finds a Mac that has receiver mode turned on.
The Mac has not granted Accessibility, so touches on this tablet cannot control it. Enable WirelessScreen under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility on the Mac.
WirelessScreen on the connecting Mac is too old for this app. Update it there to reconnect.
Or pick this %1$s under WiFi on your computer
Keep this app open. Streaming starts automatically.
Tip: shake the %1$s to open settings anytime
WirelessScreen turns this %1$s into a second screen for your Mac. It needs the WirelessScreen Mac app running on a Mac on the same WiFi network.
Install the WirelessScreen Mac app on your Mac
Join the same WiFi as your Mac
You can find this link again anytime in Settings: shake the %1$s to open it.
Automatic follows the device rotation settings. Portrait and landscape keep the receiver fixed.
Shown in the WiFi list of WirelessScreen on your computer.
The overlay shows FPS, bitrate, decode time and latency at the bottom of the screen while streaming.
What this %1$s saw while connecting: sessions, restarts, decoder trouble. No screen content and nothing leaves the %1$s unless you share it. Save the log if you need to troubleshoot a connection.
WiFi: both devices on the same network, then pick this %1$s in WirelessScreen on your computer.
Rotate the %1$s for a vertical second monitor.
Touch: tap to click, two-finger tap for right-click, drag to move, two-finger pan to scroll. Use the floating keyboard button to type from this %1$s.
Pen: draw with pressure and tilt. Fingers are ignored while the pen touches.
WirelessScreen needs the Mac app running on a Mac on the same WiFi network. Download it here if you haven\'t yet.

Android requires you to allow “Install unknown apps” for WirelessScreen before it can install the downloaded update.
